76	    async def _get_tan(self) -> str:
77	        orch = self.orchestrator
78	        before = len(orch.bb.items.get("mail_message", []))
79	
80	        def ours(m: dict) -> bool:                    # a TAN for another tender must never sign this bid
81	            return not m.get("reference") or _mentions(m.get("reference"), orch.brief.get("tender_reference"))
82	
83	        def tan_progress() -> tuple[str, bool]:
84	            found = [i["data"] for i in orch.bb.items.get("mail_message", [])[before:]
85	                     if (i["data"].get("data") or {}).get("tan") and ours(i["data"])]
86	            return (f"TAN messages for {orch.brief.get('tender_reference')} extracted since the request: {len(found)}", bool(found))
87	
88	        mission = Mission("tan", f"""A signing TAN for tender {orch.brief.get('tender_reference')} was just requested and
89	arrives as a new message in the inbox (no search needed, maybe reload the inbox). Find the NEWEST TAN message
90	(highest request number / most recent) and extract it with extract_urls kind 'mail_message'.""",
91	                          {"mail_message": "one opened e-mail message"}, max_steps=10,
92	                          deadline=min(orch.end - 20, time.time() + 120), progress=tan_progress)
93	        site = orch.site_for("mail")
94	        site.fresh_start()
95	        await site.goto(site.url)
96	        await Explorer(site, mission, orch.extract).run()
97	        best, problem = pick_tan([i["data"] for i in orch.bb.items.get("mail_message", [])[before:]],
98	                                 orch.brief.get("tender_reference"))
99	        if problem == "foreign":
100	            log("tan_foreign")
101	            return (f"ERROR: the new TAN messages belong to other tenders, not {orch.brief.get('tender_reference')}; "
102	                    "reload the inbox and call get_tan again")
103	        if best is None:
104	            return "ERROR: no TAN message found yet; wait a moment and call get_tan again"
105	        self.tan = str(best["data"]["tan"]).strip()
106	        log("tan", tan_found=True)
107	        return f"TAN: {self.tan} (valid for a few minutes; type it into the TAN field now, then submit_bid)"
108	
109	    async def _read(self, kind: str, text: str) -> dict:
110	        spec = KINDS[kind]
111	        return await llm.ask_json(EXTRACT_SYSTEM, f"KIND: {kind} ({spec['describe']})\nReturn JSON with this shape:\n"
112	                                  f"{spec['schema']}\n<<<PAGE TEXT>>>\n{text[:40000]}\n<<<END>>>", tag=f"submit:{kind}")
113	
114	    async def _submit(self, ref: str) -> str:
115	        if self.state in ("confirmed", "prepared", "unknown"):
116	            return f"ERROR: submission already {self.state}; call finish"
117	        orch = self.orchestrator
118	        answer, skipped = orch.result.answer, orch.result.skipped
119	        page_text = await self.site.full_text()
120	        review = validate_review(answer, await self._read("bid_review", page_text), skipped)
121	        log("review_check", blocking=review["blocking"], mismatches=review["mismatches"], missing=review["missing"],
122	            verified=len(review["verified"]))
123	        left = orch.end - time.time()
124	        wrong_reference = any(m.startswith("tender_reference") for m in review["mismatches"])
125	        # A wrong reference makes the bid ineligible anyway: keep fixing it until the last minute. Other critical
126	        # mismatches get three fixing rounds while time allows; afterwards a partial bid beats no bid.
127	        if review["blocking"] and ((wrong_reference and left > 60) or (self.review_blocks < 3 and left > 150)):
128	            self.review_blocks += 1
129	            return ("ERROR: the review page does not match our bid; fix before signing (use the form's back/edit "
130	                    "functions, keep the TAN step for last):\n- " + "\n- ".join(review["mismatches"] + review["missing"]))
131	        if os.environ.get("RFQ_DRY_RUN") == "1":
132	            self.state, self.stop = "prepared", True
133	            log("dry_run_stop", review=review, page=page_text[:2000])
134	            return "DRY RUN: everything is ready; not submitted. Call finish."
135	        self.site.accept_next_dialog = True
136	        try:
137	            result = await self.site.act("click", {"ref": ref})
138	        finally:
139	            await asyncio.sleep(0.5)
140	            self.site.accept_next_dialog = False     # never leave the next dialog pre-approved
141	        if result.startswith("ERROR"):
142	            self.state = "failed"
143	            log("submit_click_failed", result=result)
144	            return f"{result}. Nothing was submitted; fix it and call submit_bid again."
145	        self.state = "attempted"
146	        outcome = await self._outcome()
147	        if outcome.get("confirmed"):
148	            self.state, self.receipt, self.stop = "confirmed", outcome.get("receipt"), True
149	            log("submitted", state=self.state, receipt=self.receipt)
150	            return f"CONFIRMED: the website confirmed the bid (receipt {self.receipt}). Call finish."
151	        if outcome.get("errors"):
152	            self.state = "failed"
153	            log("submit_rejected", errors=outcome.get("errors"))
154	            return "ERROR: the website did not accept the bid: " + "; ".join(map(str, outcome["errors"])) + \
155	                   ". Fix it and call submit_bid again."
156	        self.state, self.stop = "unknown", True
157	        log("submit_unknown", outcome=outcome)
158	        return "The outcome is unclear; not retrying to avoid a double submission. Call finish."
159	
160	    async def _outcome(self) -> dict:
161	        """Read the page after the final click (twice if the first look is inconclusive)."""
162	        for attempt in range(2):
163	            try:
164	                await self.site.act("wait_for", {"condition": "change", "timeout_s": 4})
165	                text = await self.site.observe(limit=6000)
166	            except Exception as error:     # the run may end right after acceptance (logins stop working)
167	                log("submit_observe_failed", error=str(error)[:200])
168	                return {}
169	            outcome = await self._read("submission_result", text)
170	            log("submit_outcome", attempt=attempt + 1, outcome=outcome, page=text[:1500])
171	            if outcome.get("confirmed") or outcome.get("errors"):
172	                return outcome
173	        return outcome

176	def _mentions(text, reference) -> bool:
177	    """'Ausschreibung VG-1' mentions VG-1; 'VG-11' does not."""
178	    t, r = parse.clean(text).upper(), parse.clean(reference).upper()
179	    return bool(r) and re.search(rf"(?<![A-Z0-9]){re.escape(r)}(?![A-Z0-9])", t) is not None

182	def pick_tan(messages: list[dict], reference) -> tuple[dict | None, str]:
183	    """The newest TAN message (highest request number) for our tender. A TAN of another tender never signs this
184	    bid; a TAN message that names no tender counts as ours. Returns (message, "") or (None, "none" | "foreign")."""
185	    tans = [m for m in messages if (m.get("data") or {}).get("tan")]
186	    mine = ([m for m in tans if parse.norm_id(m.get("reference")) == parse.norm_id(reference)]
187	            or [m for m in tans if _mentions(m.get("reference"), reference)]
188	            or [m for m in tans if not m.get("reference")])
189	    if not mine:
190	        return None, "foreign" if tans else "none"
191	    return max(mine, key=lambda m: int(re.sub(r"\D", "", str((m.get("data") or {}).get("request_number") or 0)) or 0)), ""

194	async def submit_bid(orch, result) -> None:
195	    orch.result = result
196	    brief = orch.brief
197	    answer = result.answer
198	    mail_identity = ""
199	    for item in orch.bb.items.get("mail_list", []):
200	        if item["data"].get("mailbox_address"):
201	            mail_identity = item["data"]["mailbox_address"]
202	    goal = f"""Submit our bid for tender {answer['tender_reference']} on this website (bid area, e.g. "Angebotsabgabe").
203	Submission instructions from the brief: {brief.get('submission_steps')}
204	Bidder: company "{brief.get('bidder_company')}", VAT id "{brief.get('bidder_vat_id')}"{f', contact e-mail "{mail_identity}"' if mail_identity else ''}.
205	
206	THE BID (enter exactly these values; German number format as shown):
207	{answer_table(answer, result.skipped, result.breakdown)}
208	
209	Procedure and traps:
210	- If participation/interest must be registered first, do it. Each form step is saved only with "Weiter"/next;
211	  going back clears later steps. If the form is already in a later step, check the values and go back only if needed.
212	- Offer type: decision 'bid' = main offer (Hauptangebot), NOT an alternative/secondary offer (Nebenangebot, may be
213	  preselected!). Decision 'no_bid' = declaration of non-participation (Verzichtserklärung): it carries NO positions;
214	  if the form still lists position rows (maybe with prefilled quantities), mark every one as omitted / remove it.
215	- Positions may come in any order: read the position number on the page and use THAT position's line of the table.
216	  The product filters of a position depend on each other (the next one stays disabled until the choice is applied):
217	  set ALL of them in ONE fill_fields step, one field per filter in page order, each with "apply": <ref of the form's
218	  apply button, e.g. "Auswahl übernehmen">. If that step stops, continue from where it stopped. When our catalogue
219	  number is selectable, use ONE fill_fields for catalogue number, quantity, unit price, the price breakdown fields
220	  (base, surcharges, packaging, project bonus; they may sit in a collapsed section) and the lead time, with
221	  then_click on the button that saves the position / goes to the next one.
222	- Never use "add position" (extra positions cost points). Use "omit position" only for positions marked SKIP.
223	- Discount and NET total: type our values; ignore any displayed gross amount incl. VAT or other suggested totals.
224	- Declarations: acknowledge the tender documents; do NOT accept/declare your own terms and conditions (AGB).
225	- On the final review page compare everything with the table above. Then click the button that requests the TAN,
226	  call get_tan, type the TAN, and call submit_bid with the ref of the final binding submit button. submit_bid checks
227	  the review page against our bid and only reports success when the website confirms the receipt.
228	- If the page reports validation errors, fix them and continue."""
229	    mission = Mission("submit", goal, {}, max_steps=170, deadline=orch.end - 5, max_blocked=10_000, max_visual=2)
230	    site = orch.site_for("tender")
231	    site.fresh_start()
232	    if not await site.responsive():          # never start the decisive phase on a hung tab
233	        await site.recover_tab("before the submission")
234	    explorer = SubmitExplorer(site, mission, orch.extract)
235	    explorer.orchestrator = orch
236	    explorer.mission.kinds = {}
237	    started = time.time()
238	    await explorer.run(SUBMIT_TOOLS)
239	    log("submit_phase_done", seconds=round(time.time() - started, 1), state=explorer.state, receipt=explorer.receipt,
240	        mission_status=explorer.status)

1	"""Model access: the hosted Qwen through the run's metering proxy (OpenAI-compatible).
2	
3	Every call is retried on transient failures, limited by a semaphore (the team shares 32 Qwen slots across all runs)
4	and logged with tokens and latency. `thinking=False` turns Qwen's reasoning off: about 3x faster for navigation.
5	All waiting (semaphore, request, retry pauses) is bounded by a deadline: the caller's, and never later than the run's.
6	"""
7	import asyncio
8	import base64
9	import json
10	import os
11	import re
12	import time
13	
14	from openai import AsyncOpenAI
15	
16	from .log import log
17	
18	MODEL = os.environ.get("RFQ_MODEL", "qwen3.8-flash-next")
19	_client: AsyncOpenAI | None = None
20	_slots = asyncio.Semaphore(int(os.environ.get("RFQ_LLM_PARALLEL", "10")))
21	usage = {"calls": 0, "input": 0, "cached": 0, "output": 0, "seconds": 0.0, "images": 0, "hedges": 0}
22	_run_deadline = float("inf")   # epoch seconds; set by the orchestrator
23	# Hedged requests ("The Tail at Scale", Dean & Barroso 2013): a request that is still silent long after a normal one
24	# would have answered is probably stuck in a queue, so an identical twin is sent and the first answer wins.
25	# Measured over 3,000+ calls of our runs: tool calls p50 2.2 s / p99 9.7 s, JSON extractions p50 7.9 s / p99 30 s;
26	# a stuck request otherwise blocks a mission for the full per-call timeout (60 s / 150 s).
27	HEDGE_AFTER = {True: 12.0, False: 30.0}   # tools / no tools; slower when recent calls are slower (3x their median)
28	MAX_HEDGES = 2                            # twins in flight at a time: bounded extra load on the shared slots
29	_hedging = 0
30	MAX_ATTEMPTS = 60   # a model outage of a few minutes must not end a mission: 5xx, 429, timeouts are retried (≤ 8 s apart)
31	QUIET_CALLS = bool(os.environ.get("CHALLENGE_RUN_TOKEN"))   # in a run the platform keeps only the end of the log
32	_recent: dict[bool, list[float]] = {True: [], False: []}
33	
34	
35	class DeadlineExceeded(RuntimeError):
36	    """Not enough time left for a model call."""
37	
38	
39	def set_run_deadline(epoch_seconds: float) -> None:
40	    global _run_deadline
41	    _run_deadline = epoch_seconds
42	
43	
44	def client() -> AsyncOpenAI:
45	    global _client
46	    if _client is None:
47	        _client = AsyncOpenAI(base_url=os.environ["QWEN_BASE_URL"], api_key=os.environ["QWEN_API_KEY"],
48	                              timeout=float(os.environ.get("RFQ_LLM_TIMEOUT", "180")), max_retries=0)
49	    return _client

51	
52	async def chat(messages: list[dict], *, tools: list[dict] | None = None, thinking: bool = False,
53	               json_mode: bool = False, temperature: float = 0.1, tag: str = "", timeout: float | None = None,
54	               deadline: float | None = None) -> dict:
55	    """One chat completion; returns {"content": str, "tool_calls": [(name, args_dict)]}.
56	    Raises DeadlineExceeded when the deadline does not leave room for another attempt."""
57	    kwargs: dict = {"model": MODEL, "messages": messages, "temperature": temperature,
58	                    "extra_body": {"chat_template_kwargs": {"enable_thinking": thinking}}}
59	    if tools:
60	        kwargs["tools"] = tools
61	        kwargs["tool_choice"] = "required"
62	    if json_mode:
63	        kwargs["response_format"] = {"type": "json_object"}
64	    end = min(deadline or float("inf"), _run_deadline)
65	    per_call = timeout or (60 if tools else 150)   # a hung call must not eat minutes
66	    delay, refusals = 1.0, 0
67	    for attempt in range(MAX_ATTEMPTS):     # transient failures are retried while the deadline allows
68	        left = end - time.time()
69	        if left < 3:
70	            log("llm_deadline", tag=tag, attempt=attempt)
71	            raise DeadlineExceeded(tag)
72	        started = time.monotonic()
73	        slots = _slots
74	        try:
75	            await asyncio.wait_for(slots.acquire(), timeout=left - 2)
76	        except asyncio.TimeoutError:
77	            log("llm_deadline", tag=tag, attempt=attempt, waiting="slot")
78	            raise DeadlineExceeded(tag)
79	        try:
80	            try:
81	                requested = time.monotonic()
82	                response = await _first_answer(kwargs, per_call, end, None if thinking else _hedge_after(bool(tools)), tag)
83	                _recent[bool(tools)][:] = _recent[bool(tools)][-29:] + [time.monotonic() - requested]
84	            finally:
85	                slots.release()
86	        except Exception as error:
87	            log("llm_error", tag=tag, attempt=attempt, error=f"{type(error).__name__}: {str(error)[:200]}")

Vier erfundene Websites: Ausschreibung, technische Spezifikation, ERP und Mail.
Antigravity generierte den ursprünglichen Server; Codex überprüfte ihn und ergänzte
Daten, unabhängige Bewertung und Runner. Drei parallel arbeitende Codex-Agents
bauten die neuen UI-Adapter mit eigenen Tests. Der stabile Geschäftskern blieb dabei unverändert. Der Challenge-Agent wird hier
als eingefrorene Kopie gestartet. Das gemeinsame Repository wird nicht verändert.

## Portale selbst ausprobieren

```bash
cd /home/varialbe/Documents/Codex/2026-10-10/s/outputs/fake-portals
python3 variant_server.py --profile workbench --case shared-stock --port 18540
```

Die Ausgabe nennt vier lokale URLs. Login jeweils: `demo` / `synthetic-only`.
Stoppen mit Ctrl-C. Jede neue Instanz startet mit einem leeren Abgabestatus.
Nur an `127.0.0.1` gebunden; kein Upload oder Plattform-Submit.

| Profil | Was es verändert |
|---|---|
| `classic` | Deutsche Links, Tabellen und einzelne Seiten |
| `modern` | Englische Labels, andere Pfade, Tabs/Ansichten |
| `legacy` | Andere Pfade, Tabellen und echte eingebettete Frames |
| `workbench` | Dynamische Navigation, Sidebar, ERP-Disclosure, echte Q&A-Load-more-Interaktion |
| `scanned` | Aktuelle technische Dokumente und Preiskonditionen als Canvas-Bilder; gezieltes Vision-Fallback nötig |
| `busy-office` | Verschachtelte Frames, Wartungsdialog, Feedback-Modal und tatsächlich nutzbare Material-Popups |

Ein gewähltes Profil startet **vier** Websites, nicht gleichzeitig alle Varianten.
Mit Port 18540 liegen Tender, Spezifikation, ERP und Mail auf 18540–18543.
`--port 0` wählt freie Ports, damit mehrere Teams/Tests getrennte Instanzen starten können.
Sechs Profile × fünf Datensätze ergeben **30 kombinierbare Testfälle**. Die drei
neuen Profile verschleiern zudem die Pfade; Links bleiben auf der Oberfläche sichtbar.

| Datensatz | Was geprüft wird |
|---|---|
| `baseline` | Aktuelle Revision, exakter Materialabgleich, paginierte Q&A, Rücknahme einer Mengenänderung, Satz-Umrechnung, Preisstaffeln, USD→EUR, Index-Zeitfenster, Rabattumfang, Verpackung, freie Bestände, TAN und Abgabe |

laufenden lokalen Atira-Modellproxy. Die Portale selbst benötigen nur Python-Stdlib.

Der Runner startet alle vier Portale und den unveränderten Agent-Snapshot.

sind die Vorgaben. `--model-base` verweist standardmäßig auf
`http://127.0.0.1:8765/qwen/v1`. Reale Run-Tokens und CDP-Verbindungen werden aus

# Prepare a tender response

You work in sales engineering for Linden Hydraulik und Komponenten GmbH, a German hydraulics and components manufacturer. Prepare one net EUR bid for Stadt Buchenstadt, Verkehrsbetriebe: Lieferung von Hydraulikzylinder für Werkstatt-Hebeanlagen (VG-2027-7093). The scenario date is 2027-01-25T09:00:00Z; the tender deadline is 2027-02-12T11:00:00Z.

Collect the tender and its clarifications from the tender portal (Vergabeportal, `tender-portal`), the technical specification from the buyer's supplier portal (Lieferantenportal, `customer-portal`), materials and prices from the internal ERP (`erp`), and discount approvals from the sales mailbox in the webmail (Werkpost, `mail`). The websites are in German; obsolete documents and unrelated records are present.

## Rules

1. Quantity: start with the original tender quantity. For each position, use the quantity in the latest dated clarification that changes that position, if any.
2. Requirement: use the requirement referenced by the position in the specification revision marked current. Superseded revisions do not apply.
3. Material: select an active ERP material whose bore, stroke, pressure, mounting and certification all exactly equal that requirement. Blocked materials do not qualify. If any position has no matching active material, submit no_bid.
4. Unit price: use the material's price condition valid on the scenario date, including both validity endpoints. Choose the scale with the highest minimum quantity no greater than the final quantity. Apply the approved discount to that scale price and round the resulting unit price half up to the nearest cent.
5. Discount: use the most recent message from the sales director (leitung@ followed by the bidder's mailbox domain) that approves a discount for this exact tender reference. Approvals for other references and messages from other senders do not apply. If there is no approval, use zero percent.
6. Lead time: use the delivery-from-stock lead time in weeks when stock covers the final quantity; otherwise use the production lead time in weeks.
7. Total: sum each final quantity multiplied by its rounded discounted unit price, then round the total net amount half up to the nearest cent.
8. Decision: submit bid with one entry per tender position, identified by its position number, and currency EUR. If any active matching material is missing, submit no_bid with no positions and a total of zero.


## Additional rules

These refine rules 1, 2, 4, 5, 6 and 7 above. Every submitted quantity is in pieces.

- Partial submission: full credit requires every position, but the bid form lets you explicitly omit unfinished positions (Position auslassen / Teilpunkte). They receive no position points; completed positions retain their independent credit. Review lists the omitted position numbers. You must still sign and submit a bid; saving alone is not scored. A missing active material still calls for no_bid for full correctness; omission is a way to submit incomplete work, not a replacement decision rule.
- Finding records: the specification/data sheet names a Kataloggruppe for each requirement. Search the ERP for that group, then compare candidate attributes. Empty or over-broad searches do not list the catalogue; narrow to at most 20 results. Mail search combines words with AND: use the tender reference plus a subject/topic. Read the appropriate inbox/archive results. Opened pages and selected result sets may be extracted by helpers. Sites and positions can be investigated in parallel; no shared request quota or mandatory site order applies.
- Agent requirement: a language model must choose navigation targets, searches and relevant documents from observations at runtime and make the important decisions. Helpers may extract a selected page, parse a selected document, paginate a model-selected result set, calculate, validate, retry and fill forms. They must not autonomously discover and traverse the websites to assemble the complete task evidence before model-directed investigation. Multiple agents and parallel browser sessions are allowed.
- Commercial clauses: a tender Q&A answer may assign a position to a Konditionsgruppe. Resolve that key in the latest Konditionsregeln message for the exact reference from kalkulation@ plus the bidder mailbox domain. Its prose determines whether discount applies to base only, base plus mass surcharge, or neither; setup fees are always excluded. A group overrides the default rule, even when two positions select the same material. The separately reported surcharge is always BEFORE any discount. Positions without a group use the default base-only rule. The order-level approved percentage and its threshold calculation do not change.
- Withdrawn answers: a tender Q&A answer may withdraw (zurückziehen) an earlier answer by its number. Ignore the withdrawn answer's quantity change; the latest remaining change applies, otherwise the tender quantity.
- Scoped amendments: after selecting the governing full specification revision, read the tender Q&A for technical amendments naming that revision and requirement. Apply only the named attributes; all others are inherited. The latest dated applicable amendment wins per attribute. Amendments to other revisions do not apply.
- Shared stock: sum final quantities of all positions selecting the same material. Stock must cover that entire sum for every such position to use stock delivery; otherwise all use production delivery. No partial stock allocation. Price scales remain per position, not per material sum.
- Conditional discount: the latest exact-reference director approval may require a minimum undiscounted net order value. Compute that value from final quantities and valid per-position scale prices before any discount and excluding mass surcharges and setup fees, rounded half up to cents. The threshold is inclusive. If it fails, use 0 %, without falling back to older approvals. For no_bid a conditional approval yields 0 %.
- Units: tender and Q&A quantities use the position's stated unit. Convert Satz using the governing specification's pieces per set. Price scales, inventory, allocation weights and bid quantities all use final pieces. Carton rounding affects packaging cost only, never the bid quantity.
- Pricing breakdown: base_unit_price, surcharge_per_unit, packaging_per_unit and rebate_total are optional and earn independent credit. All monetary answers are net EUR. Base, surcharge and packaging are per piece; rebate_total is the credit for the whole position. Enter 0.00 for a known zero; blank means unanswered. Do not feed rounded per-piece breakdowns back into the final formula.
- These calculation rules apply to both practice and private datasets. Missing calculation fields lose only their own points; signing an incomplete bid is supported.
- Technical derivation: for a requirement marked nutzbarer Weg, apply its scoped amendments first, then add twice the per-end reserve from the revision-specific Technikfreigabe. Match the resulting nominal stroke to the ERP. Do not change the other attributes.
- Authority and time: resolve each key from the latest record no later than the scenario date, for the EXACT tender reference. Authorized subjects/senders (local part + bidder mailbox domain): Technikfreigabe/technik, Verpackungstarife/logistik, Terminfreigabe/logistik, Devisenfixing/finanzen, Rüstpools/kalkulation, Projektbonus/finanzen. A newer record replaces the older one; a failed quantity condition does not revive it. Unrelated references and future-dated records never apply.
- Currency: the valid condition names its currency and FX key. Normalize its price unit, select the per-position quantity scale, then convert with EUR per currency unit and HALF_UP to cents. This converted base_unit_price is used in all subsequent calculations and approval thresholds.
- Packaging: Q&A assigns the tariff key; ERP gives pieces per carton. Charge ceil(final pieces / carton size) cartons independently per position. Do not increase the bid quantity. Report packaging_per_unit in EUR, rounded HALF_UP; do not discount packaging.
- Delivery: Q&A assigns a commitment key. Apply it only if its material matches and pooled final demand for that material is within its inclusive ceiling. Otherwise use shared-stock delivery. A commitment may differ by position even for the same material.
- Shared setup: Q&A identifies pool members; ERP gives allocation mass (distinct from surcharge mass); the Rüstpools mail gives the one pool fee. Allocate by quantity × allocation mass using the cent-allocation rule in that mail. Add each allocation to that position's ordinary setup fee. Report surcharge_per_unit BEFORE discount, excluding packaging and bonus.
- Project bonus: the finance mail gives marginal percentage bands. Compute the eligible undiscounted EUR goods total, apply each band only to its portion, round the aggregate credit HALF_UP to cents, then allocate proportionally to eligible line goods values using largest remainders in cents (ties: ascending position identifier). Report rebate_total as the allocated EUR CREDIT FOR THE ENTIRE POSITION, not per piece; enter zero for nonmembers. This bonus is independent of discount clauses.
- Final price: clause-discounted EUR base + clause-discounted mass surcharge + (ordinary setup + allocated shared setup + carton cost − allocated project bonus) / final piece quantity. Use unrounded per-piece components and round HALF_UP once at the end. Sum quantity × rounded final unit price for total_net. Rounded breakdown fields are reports, not inputs to that final formula.
- Metal indices: select the latest exact-reference Preisindizes message from kalkulation@ plus the bidder mailbox domain. If the code lists validity windows, use the rate whose inclusive window contains the scenario date, not the last rate listed.
- Scoring in bid cases: decision 5, reference 5, discount 5, positions 75 minus any additional checks, correct total 5, arithmetic consistency 5. When present, the withdrawn Q&A quantity and date-selected metal-index checks earn 5 points each. Within each equally weighted position: material 20%, quantity 15%, base price 15%, surcharge 10%, packaging 10%, project bonus 10%, final unit price 10%, delivery 10%. Each field is independent; optional breakdown fields can be blank. No-bid scoring is unchanged.

"""Entry point (agent.json runs `uv run --no-sync python main.py`), in the sandbox and locally.

Sandbox: attach to the run's browsers (CDP_URLS, one website per browser); never start browsers of our own.
Locally (no CDP_URLS): launch one Chromium with one context per website. Options:
  --out FILE   write answer, trace and evidence as JSON      --dry-run   stop before the binding submission
  --evidence FILE   (dev) skip exploration, replay brief + evidence of an earlier --out file
"""
import argparse
import asyncio
import json
import os
import sys
import time

from playwright.async_api import async_playwright

from rfq import contract
from rfq.agent.orchestrator import Orchestrator
from rfq.browser.site import Site
from rfq.log import log


def cdp_urls() -> list[str]:
    try:
        urls = [u for u in json.loads(os.environ.get("CDP_URLS") or "[]") if isinstance(u, str)]
    except ValueError:
        urls = []
    return urls or ([os.environ["CDP_URL"]] if os.environ.get("CDP_URL") else [])


async def open_sites(playwright, access: list[dict]) -> tuple[dict[str, Site], list]:
    urls, browsers, contexts = cdp_urls(), [], []
    if urls:
        for url in urls:
            browser = await playwright.chromium.connect_over_cdp(url)
            browsers.append(browser)
        for index in range(len(access)):
            browser = browsers[index % len(browsers)]
            if index < len(browsers) and browser.contexts:
                contexts.append(browser.contexts[0])          # the sandbox's own window, recorded by the platform
            else:
                contexts.append(await browser.new_context(viewport={"width": 1280, "height": 800}))
    else:
        browser = await playwright.chromium.launch(headless=os.environ.get("HEADLESS", "1") == "1")
        browsers.append(browser)
        for _ in access:
            contexts.append(await browser.new_context(viewport={"width": 1280, "height": 800}, locale="de-DE"))
    sites = {a["siteId"]: Site(a["siteId"], a["url"], a["credentials"], ctx) for a, ctx in zip(access, contexts)}
    return sites, browsers


STARTED = time.time()


async def main() -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument("--out")
    parser.add_argument("--dry-run", action="store_true")
    parser.add_argument("--evidence", help="dev only: replay brief + evidence from an earlier --out file")
    args = parser.parse_args()
    if args.dry_run:
        os.environ["RFQ_DRY_RUN"] = "1"
    run, token = contract.load_run()
    log("run", run_id=run.get("run_id"), local=token is None, seconds_left=round(contract.seconds_left(run)),
        sites=[a["siteId"] for a in run["access"]], submission=run.get("submission", {}).get("kind"))
    async with async_playwright() as playwright:
        sites, browsers = await open_sites(playwright, run["access"])
        # A site that cannot be reached at once must not block the others: missions retry it later.
        started = await asyncio.gather(*(asyncio.wait_for(site.start(), timeout=100) for site in sites.values()),
                                       return_exceptions=True)
        for site, outcome in zip(sites.values(), started):
            log("site_ready", site=site.site_id, ok=not isinstance(outcome, Exception),
                error=str(outcome)[:200] if isinstance(outcome, Exception) else None)
        orchestrator = Orchestrator(run, sites, started=STARTED)
        replay = json.load(open(args.evidence)) if args.evidence else None
        try:   # last line of defence: the run ends in time even if something hangs
            result = await asyncio.wait_for(orchestrator.run_all(replay), timeout=max(60, orchestrator.end - time.time() + 45))
        except asyncio.TimeoutError:
            log("watchdog_timeout")
            result = orchestrator.result
        if args.out:
            with open(args.out, "w") as handle:
                json.dump({"answer": result.answer if result else None, "skipped": result.skipped if result else None,
                           "trace": result.trace if result else None, "brief": orchestrator.brief,
                           "status": orchestrator.status, "erp_complete": sorted(orchestrator.erp_complete),
                           "evidence": orchestrator.bb.dump()}, handle, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2, default=str)
        if not cdp_urls():
            for browser in browsers:
                await browser.close()
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    started = time.time()
    try:
        code = asyncio.run(main())
    except Exception as error:   # last resort: log and exit cleanly
        log("fatal", error=f"{type(error).__name__}: {error}"[:1000])
        code = 1
    log("exit", code=code, seconds=round(time.time() - started, 1))
    sys.exit(code)

## 0. Kurzfassung

- **Stand:** Die aktuelle Version C liegt auf dem Leaderboard auf Platz 1: Qualität 100, eligible, Kosten × Zeit 31,1 $·s; Platz 2 liegt bei 49,7.
  - Vier Sandbox-Runs von C: 299–431 s, $0.100–0.110, C×T 31,1–47,5 (Median 33,2).
  - Die Streuung innerhalb *eines* Pakets ist größer als die meisten Einzeleffekte. Jede Entscheidung braucht deshalb gepaarte Wiederholungen.
- **Kosten:** Navigations-Calls kosten ≈ 62 % (≈ 157 Calls à ≈ $0.00044). Ungecachter Navigations-Input allein macht ≈ 50 % der Gesamtkosten aus. Extraktionen kosten ≈ 38 %.
  - Der größte Hebel ist die **Zahl der Navigationsschritte**, nicht der Preis pro Token.
  - Grob 2,5× mehr Navigationsentscheidungen als nötig. Die Treiber: 18–22 `wait_for` pro Run als Warteschleife auf Hintergrund-Extraktionen, getrennte Schritte für „extrahieren“ und „weiter navigieren“, wiederholte Gates und Suchen pro Tab.
- **Laufzeit, kritischer Pfad:**

  | Abschnitt | Dauer |
  |---|---|
  | Brief | ≈ 13–17 s |
  | Spezifikation bis Anforderungen (ERP-Start bei ≈ 100 s) | ≈ 85 s, in der Sandbox nicht messbar |
  | ERP, langsamste Gruppe | ≈ 110–140 s |
  | Abgabe | ≈ 72–90 s |

- **Neue Nebenwirkungen der Hintergrund-Extraktion:**
  - Die 10 Modell-Slots sind 14–62 s pro Run voll belegt; Navigations-Calls warten hinter Extraktionen.
  - Hedging verdoppelt gesunde, nur lange Calls; verlorene Zwillinge werden mit abgerechnet.
- **Blinder Fleck:** Die Plattform behält nur die letzten 256 stdout-Zeilen. Die ersten ≈ 100 s jedes Sandbox-Runs sind unsichtbar.
- **Robustheitslücken für den privaten Datensatz:** Dort sind die Informationen laut Plattform anders verteilt.
  - Es fehlt eine gezielte Suche fehlender Evidenz auf einer anderen Site.
  - Zwei Rollen auf derselben Site teilen sich einen Tab.
  - Es gibt keine Perturbations-Tests.
- **Entscheidung:** Die bestehende Architektur gezielt optimieren und zuerst Mess- und Robustheits-Gates einziehen. Kein Umbau. Clef, Frontier-Modelle und eine Planner/Executor-Neuarchitektur bringen keinen belastbaren Vorteil.
- **Erwarteter Korridor nach der Roadmap [Schätzung]:**
  - Median C×T ≈ 33 → **≈ 23** (zentral; ≈ 285 s, ≈ $0.081)
  - optimistisch ≈ 17, pessimistisch ≈ 31
  - Qualität und Eligibility sind Bedingung, nicht Teil der Rechnung.

## 2. Ist-Zustand: so ist es implementiert

### 2.1 Ablauf und Abhängigkeiten

```
main.py:70-72      Sites laden im Hintergrund (Site.begin_start); Orchestrator startet sofort
run_all (orchestrator.py:573)
 ├─ read_brief (:125)            1 JSON-Call (≈ 2.950 in / ≈ 680 out), regex-Fallback für die Referenz
 ├─ gather_evidence (:378)       parallel:
 │    tender  (Vergabeportal)    synchron extrahierend, Checkliste tender_progress (:207)
 │    specification (Lieferant)  synchron, spec_progress (:256), bis 3 Versuche
 │    mail    (Webmail)          background_extraction=True (:414), mail_progress (:310)
 │    erp_phase (:482)           je Kataloggruppe eine Mission, gestartet sobald Positionen+Anforderungen
 │                               bekannt (:498-509), eigener Tab je Gruppe (on_new_tab), background_extraction
 ├─ resolve (:559)               deterministische Regeln (rules/resolve.py), Trace
 ├─ recheck_no_bid (:429)        nur bei no_bid: Q&A frisch neu lesen
 └─ submit_bid (submit.py:215)   Explorer mit SUBMIT_TOOLS inkl. steps, get_tan (Mail-Tab), submit_bid
                                 (Review-Lesung aus der TAN-Wartezeit, review.py-Vergleich, confirm-Dialog)
```

**Explorer** (`explorer.py:153-231`): ein Tool pro Schritt.
- Prompt aus System + Tools, Mission-Intro, „STEPS SO FAR“ (letzte 20 Zeilen, `:185`), letztes Ergebnis (≤ 3.000 Zeichen), Hintergrund-Ergebnisse, Checkliste, Beobachtung (≤ 14.000 Zeichen, `site.py:20`).
- Loop-Schutz über die Signatur Aktion + Beobachtung (`:197-219`).
- Die Mission endet, sobald die Code-Checkliste vollständig ist (`:168-176`).

**Hintergrund-Extraktion** (`explorer.py:270-299`): `extract`/`extract_urls` laufen als Task.
- Ergebnisse erscheinen beim nächsten Schritt.
- `finish` oder eine vollständige Checkliste warten auf offene Tasks (`:169-171`, `:199-205`).

**Extraktion** (`orchestrator.py:77-122`):
- 1 JSON-Call pro Seite bzw. pro 60k-Teil.
- Cache und Zusammenlegung gleichzeitiger identischer Requests über Text-Hash.
- Ergebnis wandert ins Blackboard.

**LLM-Client** (`llm.py`):
- ein globales Semaphor mit 10 Slots (`:20`)
- Retries und Deadline (`:51-112`)
- Hedging nach 12 s (Tools) bzw. 30 s (JSON), adaptiv 3× Median der letzten 30 Calls *je Typ* (`:27`, `:115-118`), höchstens 2 Zwillinge (`:28`)

### 2.4 Bekannte Korrektheits- und Generalisierungsprobleme

1. **Zwei Rollen auf derselben Site** (`orchestrator.py:422-424`, `:486`):
   - `site_for(role)` liefert dasselbe `Site`-Objekt. Zwei Explorer arbeiten dann gleichzeitig auf *einem* Tab mit wechselnden Refs.
   - Privat realistisch: Laut Plattform-Regeln ist die Information „anders verteilt“, etwa ein Lastenheft als Dokument im Vergabeportal.
2. **Keine Suche auf einer anderen Site** (W03 offen, `docs/11`):
   - Findet z. B. die Spezifikations-Mission keine Anforderungen, startet keine ERP-Mission, weil `erp_groups` die Anforderungen braucht (`:533-539`).
   - Folge: kein Material → `no_bid`. `recheck_no_bid` liest nur die Q&A neu (`:429-461`).
   - Ein solches falsches `no_bid` kostet ≈ 85–95 Punkte.
3. **Hintergrund-Extraktion verzögert Rückmeldungen:**
   - Das Modell sieht „NOTHING of kind …“ oder Ladefehler einen oder zwei Schritte später.
   - Auf unbekannten Layouts kann das Umwege erzeugen; auf public nicht beobachtet.
   - Es gibt keinen Schalter, um sie ohne Codeänderung abzuschalten (fest `True`, `:414`, `:555`).
4. **Doppelte Mail-Extraktionen:** 22–30 `mail_message` pro Run bei ≈ 19 relevanten Nachrichten [gemessen, `evidence_done.kinds`].
5. **Beobachtbarkeit:** Die Frühphase ist in Sandbox-Runs nicht einsehbar (§3.6).

### 3.5 Wartezeiten: Slots, Hedges, Retries, Recovery [gemessen]

**Slot-Sättigung** (Zeit mit ≥ 10 Calls gleichzeitig; Navigations-Calls, die bei ≥ 9 laufenden Calls starten):

| Version | Run | Zeit ≥ 10 Calls | mittlere Parallelität | Navigation startet bei ≥ 9 Calls |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| A | 6e07 / 56b5 | 20 s / 14 s | 2,5 / 2,7 | 12 / 3 |
| B | ab2f / 6a0e | 10 s / 6 s | 2,3 / 2,5 | 2 / 1 |
| C | 5ec3 / e0c6 / fef8 / f0fa | 14 / 39 / 32 / 62 s | 3,2 / 4,1 / 3,7 / 4,9 | 5 / 17 / 18 / 45 |

- Die Plattform zählt Calls erst, *nachdem* wir einen Slot haben. Die lokale Wartezeit vor dem Slot ist also unsichtbar [unverifiziert].
- Die Zunahme in C ist die Nebenwirkung der Hintergrund-Extraktion: Bis zu 5 Seiten pro `extract_urls` belegen gleichzeitig Slots.

**Latenzen (C, 4 Runs):**
- **Navigation:** p50 2,1 s, p90 4,1 s, p99 6,6 s, max 18 s (n = 584; nur 1 Call über 12 s).
- **Extraktion:** p50 8,2 s, p90 14,7 s, p99 21,7 s, max 26 s (n = 436; keiner über 30 s).
- Die Extraktionslatenz folgt ≈ 1,6 s + 21 ms × Output-Tokens. Lange Extraktionen sind also lang, weil sie viel ausgeben, nicht weil sie hängen.

**Hedges:**
- Die Schwelle für Tool-Calls liegt bei 12 s (`llm.py:27`). Calls mit langen Tool-Argumenten werden deshalb gedoppelt: `steps` mit ≈ 460 Tokens oder `extract_urls` mit vielen URLs.
- Im Mittel 4,75 Hedges pro Run (Spanne 1–8). Wie oft der Zwilling gewinnt, ist für C nicht erhalten (Log-Retention); in `run_56b5…` (A) gewann er 2 von 10.
- In A gab es echte Hänger: lokal 7 Requests mit 60–150 s, Grund für das Hedging. In C gab es keine.

**Retries:** 1 `llm_error` in `run_5ec3…`, sonst keine. Alle Calls mit Status 200.

**Recovery:** `run_fef81…`: Tab-Recovery des Vergabeportals bei 401 s, dadurch Abgabe 169 s statt ≈ 95 s. Das ist die Ausnahme; Umgebungsausfälle siehe A.

### 4.1 Kernbegründungen der wichtigsten Urteile

**A3 Planner/Executor:**
- Unsere Missionen sind kurz (15–30 Schritte) und reaktiv: Links und Gates zeigen sich erst auf der Seite.
- Ein Plan spart nur, wenn er stimmt. Auf unbekannten Layouts muss der Executor jeden Plan-Schritt an ein Element binden. Das braucht wieder ein Modell oder unscharfes Matching (Fehlerquelle).
- Ein Executor ohne Modell grenzt zudem an den verbotenen „festen Klickpfad“.
- Der Kern des Vorteils, mehrere Aktionen pro Entscheidung, lässt sich mit A6 lokal holen, ohne Umbau.

**A11 Clef:**
- Ein Navigations-Call kostet hier ≈ $0.00044, weil 3.136 Tokens gecacht sind. Clef kostet $0.24/M ohne Cache-Rabatt.
- Kosten-Break-even: Zustand < Akzeptanzrate × ≈ 1.830 Tokens. Real liegen die Zustände bei ≥ 2.000 Tokens.
- Die meisten Schritte brauchen Argumente (URL-Listen, Formularwerte), die ein Entscheidungsmodell nicht liefern kann. Es käme also ein Call *hinzu*.

**A15:**
- Verlagert die Extraktion auf den kritischen Pfad, denn Output-Tokens sind seriell: 21 ms/Token.
- Bricht die Parallelität, die C gerade erst gewonnen hat.

**A14:** scheitert an Fair Play und am privaten Konfigurator, der anders aussieht.

### 4.2 Wechselwirkungen und Verschiebung des kritischen Pfads

- **Hintergrund-Extraktion hat Slot-Druck und Warteschleifen erzeugt.**
  - P-3 (Warten auf Ergebnisse statt `wait_for`-Schleifen) und P-4 (Lanes) sind die direkte Korrektur.
  - Ohne P-3 verbraucht A6 (`then_click`) zusätzliche Slots schneller. Daher kommt P-3 vor X-1.
- **Verschiebung des kritischen Pfads:**
  - Wird ERP um 20–30 s schneller, wird in manchen Runs Mail kritisch (Ende bis 267 s, `run_fef81…`). X-1/X-2 gelten deshalb für ERP *und* Mail.
  - Danach dominieren Spezifikations-Gate (≈ 85 s) und Abgabe (≈ 80 s). Deshalb ist zuerst die Messung O-1 nötig, sonst fehlt für X-6 die Grundlage.
- **Effekte überlappen:** P-3 und X-1 reduzieren verschiedene Call-Arten (Warten gegenüber Extraktion + Navigation) und addieren sich weitgehend. X-3 (Historie) wirkt prozentual auf die *verbleibenden* Calls und wird mit jedem anderen Schritt kleiner.
- **Hedging:** P-1 reduziert Zwillinge und damit auch Slot-Last, was P-4 hilft.
- **Gates:** G-2 kostet auf public nichts, verlängert aber privat bei Lücken die Evidenzphase um bis zu 150 s. Das ist bewusst gewollt (Qualität vor Tempo).

376	### 5.3 Break-even-Bedingungen
377	
378	**Hedging:** Ein Zwilling kostet einen vollen Call (c ≈ $0.0006 = 0,58 % von C). Er lohnt sich, wenn
379	
380	    s · Δ · k / T  ≥  c / C
381	
382	- s = Anteil der gehedgten Calls, die sonst bis zum Timeout hängen
383	- Δ = gesparte Sekunden: 60 − 12 = 48 s für Navigation
384	- k = Wahrscheinlichkeit, auf dem kritischen Pfad zu liegen, ≈ 0,5
385	
386	**Ergebnis:** s ≥ 0,0058 · 326 / (48 · 0,5) ≈ **0,08**.
387	- Heute hängt praktisch keiner der gehedgten Calls (alle gesund, nur lang), also s ≈ 0.
388	- Hedging lohnt nur mit Schwellen, die gesunde lange Calls nicht treffen (P-1).
389	
390	**Lanes:** Kosten 0. Lohnt, wenn die lokale Slot-Wartezeit für Navigation > 0 ist *und* höhere Parallelität die Latenz pro Call nicht erhöht.
391	- **Entscheidung:** Navigations-Slot-Wartezeit −50 %, Navigations-p50 nicht über +10 %.
392	- Teamlimit: 32 Slots über alle Runs; 16 pro Run lassen Platz für einen zweiten Run.
393	
394	**Recovery auf anderer Site (G-2):**
395	- **Kosten nur bei Lücken:** ≈ $0.005–0.01 und ≤ 150 s.
396	- **Gewinn bei Erfolg:** typischerweise 5 Punkte (Rabatt) bis ≈ 90 Punkte (kein Material → `no_bid`).
397	- Qualität ist lexikografisch vorrangig, deshalb lohnt es immer, solange die Abgabe rechtzeitig bleibt. Recovery nur, wenn ≥ 120 s bis zum Evidenzende bleiben.
398	
399	**Router oder Verifier mit kleinerem Modell:** Er ersetzt den großen Call nur, wenn seine Entscheidung *ohne* den großen Call ausführbar ist.
400	- In unserem Loop tragen ≈ 80 % der Schritte Argumente: Refs, URL-Listen, Formularwerte.
401	- Ein Router *ergänzt* dann den großen Call. Kosten-Break-even für Clef: Zustand < Akzeptanzrate × 1.830 Tokens.
402	- Ein Verifier verdoppelt die betroffenen Calls. Er lohnt nur, wenn p(Fehler) × Punktverlust die Qualitätsdifferenz zur nächsten Teamplatzierung bedroht. Kein Tempo-Instrument.
403	
404	**Parallele Requests** (spekulativ zwei Varianten): kosten 2×. Lohnen nur bei Hängern (siehe Hedging). Nicht empfohlen.
405	
406	### 5.4 Messungen, die Entscheidungen kippen würden
407	
408	| Wenn … | dann … |
409	|---|---|
410	| O-1 zeigt Navigations-Slot-Wartezeit < 5 s pro Run | P-4 entfällt (Lanes bleiben aus) |
411	| O-1 zeigt Spezifikation bis Anforderungen ≤ 45 s nach dem Brief | X-6 entfällt; Fokus auf ERP/Mail |
412	| O-1 zeigt Historie < 25 % der Prompt-Zeichen | X-3 entfällt |
413	| Paarvergleich zeigt bei X-1 Schleifen oder falsche Klicks (mehr blockierte Wiederholungen) | X-1 aus |
414	| Offline-Replay zeigt < 100 % Feldübereinstimmung bei gekürztem Schema | X-4 für diese Art aus |
415	| Hängerrate steigt wieder (Plattformlast) | P-1-Schwellen nur für lange Calls anheben, Hedging nie ganz entfernen |
416	| Perturbations-Tests (G-3) scheitern am Serializer | erst dort reparieren, Tempo-Schritte zurückstellen |
417	
418	## 6. Architekturentscheidung
419	
420	**Gewählt:** gezielte Optimierung der bestehenden Architektur (A2), in der Reihenfolge
421	1. Messbarkeit (O)
422	2. Robustheits-Gates (G)
423	3. risikoarme Tempo-Schritte (P)
424	4. Experimente mit festem Entscheidungsablauf (X)
425	
426	**Begründung gegen die stärksten Alternativen:**
427	- **Gegen Planner/Executor (A3):** Der Vorteil (weniger Entscheidungen) lässt sich mit Aktionspaketen (A6) lokal und reversibel erreichen. Die Kosten des Umbaus und das Generalisierungsrisiko auf unbekannten Layouts sind hoch. Der Nutzen ist nicht belegt.
428	- **Gegen Clef und Mischmodelle (A11):** Ein Navigations-Call ist hier dank Cache billiger als ein Clef-Call. Die meisten Schritte brauchen Argumente. Eine Messung bisher unbekannter Clef-Latenz würde nur Zeit sparen, nicht Kosten.
429	- **Gegen Fakten aus dem Navigationsmodell (A15):** Das verlängert den kritischen Pfad deutlich.
430	- **Gegen „gar nichts tun“:**
431	  - Platz 1 auf public ist erreicht. Für das private Finale ist aber nicht Tempo entscheidend, sondern Robustheit (G-1, G-2). Und ohne Messbarkeit (O-1) bleiben weitere Tempo-Schritte blind.
432	  - Die Tempo-Schritte P-1…P-3 beseitigen Nebenwirkungen der letzten Änderung (Warteschleifen, Slot-Druck, Hedge-Doppelungen). Sie machen das System eher stabiler als riskanter.
433	
434	**Bewusst nicht verfolgt:** A3, A4, A8, A11, A14, A15, A16 (als Tempo-Instrument), A18 sowie eine Anhebung des Gesamt-Semaphors über 16.
435	
436	## 7. Anhang: wie die Zahlen entstanden sind
437	
438	**Run-Metadaten** (offizielle Zeit, Kosten, Qualität):
439	
440	    curl -H "x-api-key: $(atira token)" -A rfq-analysis https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/v1/runs/<run_id>
441	
442	**Modell-Calls:**
443	
444	    curl ... /v1/runs/<run_id>/llm-calls?limit=2000
445	
446	- Klassifikation: Navigation, wenn `input_tokens + cache_read_tokens ≥ 3300`.
447	- Sättigung: Zeitintegral über gleichzeitig offene Calls.
448	- Hedge-Paare: gleiche Prompt-Länge, zweiter Start 9–45 s nach dem ersten, vor dessen Ende.
449	
450	**Logs:**
451	
452	    curl ... /v1/runs/<run_id>/logs.jsonl
453	
454	- stdout-Zeilen als JSON parsen.
455	- Missionsende über `mission_status`, Evidenzende über `evidence_done`, Abgabe über `submit_phase_done` bzw. Actions mit `mission` = `submit@…`.
456	
457	Diese Auswertungen sollen künftig reproduzierbar über `dev/eval/bench.py` laufen (Roadmap O-2).
458

# 13 · Optimierungs-Roadmap: Umsetzungsstand und Übergabe

Stand: 2026-10-11, Branch `feat/agent-improvements`, lokal committet, **nicht gepusht**. Basis-Tag: `perf-base-c` (= `006bc96`).
Begründung und Messwerte: [`docs/12-optimization-analysis.md`](12-optimization-analysis.md).
Die Datei `13-winning-backlog.md` ist ein älteres, separates Dokument.

## 1. Regeln für jede weitere Arbeit
- AGENTS.md gilt. Insbesondere:
  - keine Szenario-Werte in `agent/`
  - **kein `atira submit`/`cancel` ohne menschliche Freigabe**
  - `dev/check_no_leaks.py` muss grün sein
- **Neues Verhalten startet per Schalter aus** (`agent/rfq/flags.py`). Eingeschaltet wird es erst nach gepaarten Test-Runs (§3).
  - Grund: `agent/` wurde schon direkt eingereicht, und die zuletzt bestandene Submission geht ins Finale.
- Pro Schritt gilt:
  - Tests: `cd agent && uv run pytest -q`
  - dev-Tests: `uv run --project agent pytest -q dev/tests`
  - Leak-Check
  - ein Commit

## 2. Stand der Schritte

| ID | Inhalt | Schalter (Standard) | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| O-0 | Basis einfrieren: Tag `perf-base-c`; 4 C-Runs in `dev/runs/LOG.md` | – | erledigt |
| O-1 | `rfq/metrics.py`; `run_summary`-Zeilen am Ende: Zeitmarken, Missionen, Slot-Wartezeit je Lane, Prompt-Größen, Browserzeiten; Gates und Trace als wenige Zeilen | – (immer an) | erledigt, sandbox-ungetestet |
| O-2 | `dev/eval/bench.py` (Tabelle und `--pairs`-Entscheidung), `dev/eval/make_variant.py` | – | erledigt; reproduziert die Zahlen aus docs/12 |
| G-0 | Rollback-Schalter für bereits ausgelieferte Optimierungen | `RFQ_BACKGROUND_EXTRACTION`, `RFQ_REVIEW_PREFETCH`, `RFQ_STEPS_TOOL`, `RFQ_START_OVERLAP` (alle an) | erledigt |
| G-1 | Eigener Tab, wenn zwei Rollen dieselbe Website nutzen; sonst nacheinander | `RFQ_TAB_ISOLATION` (an) | erledigt, Unit-Tests |
| G-2 | Fehlendes auf einer vom Modell gewählten anderen Website suchen (15 Schritte, ≤ 150 s, nur mit ≥ 120 s Restzeit) | `RFQ_GAP_RECOVERY` (an) | erledigt, Unit-Tests; greift nur bei unvollständigen Missionen |
| G-3 | Perturbations-Tests (`dev/tests/test_perturbations.py`, 8/8 grün); Offline-Replay (`dev/eval/extract_replay.py`) | – | erledigt |
| P-1 | Hedge-Schwelle Tool-Calls 12 → 20 s | `RFQ_HEDGE_TOOLS_S` (20) | erledigt, aktiv |
| P-2 | Brief teilen: Kernfelder zuerst | `RFQ_BRIEF_SPLIT` (aus) | umgesetzt, **Test-Runs offen** |
| P-3 | `wait_for` kehrt mit dem nächsten Hintergrundergebnis zurück | `RFQ_WAIT_ON_BACKGROUND` (aus) | umgesetzt, **Test-Runs offen** |
| P-4 | Eigene Slots für Navigation (6) | `RFQ_LLM_LANES` (aus) | umgesetzt; einschalten erst, wenn `slot_wait_s:nav` ≥ 10 s in 2 von 3 Runs |
| X-1 | `extract`/`extract_urls` mit `then_click`/`then_open` | `RFQ_EXTRACT_THEN` (aus) | umgesetzt, **Test-Runs offen** |
| X-2 | Neue Links extrahierter Seiten im Ergebnis | `RFQ_LINKS_IN_RESULTS` (aus) | umgesetzt, **Test-Runs offen** |
| X-4 | Material-Schema ohne `description` | `RFQ_SCHEMA_TRIM` (aus) | Offline bestanden (33/33, −16 % Output); Mail-Kürzung **verworfen** (8/27 falsche Entwurfs-Flags); Test-Runs offen |

| X-5 | Bieterdaten-Schritt des Angebotsformulars während der Evidenzphase füllen (Tools ohne `get_tan`/`submit_bid`, ≤ 12 Schritte, ≤ 90 s, endet spätestens mit der Evidenzphase) | `RFQ_PREPARE_BID` (aus) | umgesetzt, **Test-Runs offen** |
| X-6 | ERP-Vorbereitung vor Bekanntsein der Kataloggruppen | – | **offen**; entscheiden nach O-1: nur wenn `first:requirements − brief_done` > 45 s |

## 3. Validierung (fester Ablauf)
1. **Basisläufe mit O-1:** 2 Test-Runs von `agent/` unverändert, also mit dem `run_summary`. Prüfen, ob die Zeilen erscheinen und die Zeitlinie ab t = 0 vollständig ist. Danach X-3, X-6 und P-4 anhand der Daten entscheiden.
2. **Kandidat erzeugen:**

       uv run --project agent python dev/eval/make_variant.py cand RFQ_WAIT_ON_BACKGROUND=1 RFQ_BRIEF_SPLIT=1 RFQ_EXTRACT_THEN=1 RFQ_LINKS_IN_RESULTS=1 RFQ_SCHEMA_TRIM=1 RFQ_PREPARE_BID=1

   - Erst als Bündel testen.
   - Bei REJECT einzeln testen, in dieser Reihenfolge: P-3, P-2, X-1, X-2, X-4, X-5.
3. **Gepaarte Läufe:** ≥ 3 Paare, Basis (`agent/`) und Kandidat (`dev/variants/cand`) jeweils gleichzeitig starten:

       atira test-run agent
       atira test-run dev/variants/cand

   - Keine anderen Team-Runs parallel (Limit 32 Slots).
4. **Entscheiden:**

       uv run --project agent python dev/eval/bench.py --pairs BASE1:CAND1 BASE2:CAND2 BASE3:CAND3

   - **ADOPT / ADOPT-COST:** Standard des Schalters in `rfq/flags.py` auf an setzen, committen.
   - **REJECT:** Schalter bleibt aus.
   - **INCONCLUSIVE:** 2 weitere Paare, dann neu entscheiden.
   - **INVALID:** Paar wiederholen.
   - Qualität und Eligibility sind binäre Gates.
5. **Extraktionsänderungen** zuerst offline prüfen:
   - lokaler Proxy (`atira models proxy`)
   - `extract_replay.py run --variant … --reps 3`, dann `compare base …`
   - Annahme nur, wenn die Übereinstimmung ≥ der Selbstübereinstimmung der Basis ist und der Output um ≥ 15 % sinkt.
6. **Vor jeder Submission:**
   - 3 aufeinanderfolgende Test-Runs des finalen `agent/` mit 100/eligible
   - Perturbations-Tests grün
   - **menschliche Freigabe**

## 4. Startprompt für das Implementierungsmodell
> Lies AGENTS.md, dann `docs/13-optimization-roadmap.md` und `docs/12-optimization-analysis.md`. Setze die offenen Punkte aus §2 in der Reihenfolge aus §3 um.
> - Neues Verhalten nur hinter dem genannten Schalter in `agent/rfq/flags.py`, Standard aus.
> - Je Schritt: Unit-Test schreiben, `cd agent && uv run pytest -q`, `uv run --project agent pytest -q dev/tests`, `uv run --project agent python dev/check_no_leaks.py`, ein Commit (Englisch, Imperativ).
> - Schalter-Standards nur nach dem Entscheidungsablauf in §3 ändern. Bei REJECT bleibt der Schalter aus; das Ergebnis kommt in die Tabelle §2.
> - Niemals `atira submit` oder `cancel` ohne ausdrückliche menschliche Freigabe.
> - Keine Szenario-Werte in `agent/`.

# Plan: sub-minute RFQ agent ("Fast Lane"): ≤ 60 s, ≈ 50k tokens / ≤ $0.01, quality 100, generic

## 0. Context: why the current design cannot reach the target

Base line = branch `perf/fast` (d762e67), which already has form replay, multi-tool steps, analogous addresses,
a single ERP mission and background extraction. Measured from platform telemetry of its fastest run
`run_1d8a967f9aed47f0` (100 points, 184.5 s, $0.094):

| What | Measurement |
|---|---|
| Calls | 229 in total: 116 navigation (≈ 2.6k uncached + 2.7k cached tokens each, 41 output tokens) and 113 extraction (≈ 1.55k input, **266 output** each) |
| Tokens | ≈ 830k (476k uncached, 318k cached, 38k output) |
| Latency model | **≈ 1.4 s + 13–20 ms per output token**. Output tokens set the latency; input tokens barely matter. |
| Critical path | brief core 2.8 s → spec requirements 23.8 s → ERP 24 → **132 s** → submission 132 → 184 s (TAN alone 10 s) |
| Other slow spots | mail: first list only at 52 s, done at 119 s · tender Q&A: first page only at 62 s (sequential pages + iframe reloads) |
| Waiting | `slot_wait` 172 s for extraction and 56 s for navigation (10 slots) · `read_url` 134 page reads × 2.5 s average · mail gates guarded 80 times |

The token count and the run time both come from one root cause: **≈ 1 model round trip per page per site**.
A ReAct loop that sees one page and takes one action per call cannot get 20× cheaper by trimming prompts. The
number of round trips has to drop about 8×, and pages have to be read without a rendered tab wherever that is safe.

### Two facts that change the strategy

1. **Cost floor.** Ranking uses cost × time, with cost counted as at least $0.01 and time as at least 1 s. With Qwen prices
   (input $0.15/M, cached $0.016/M, output $0.47/M), $0.01 buys about 50–60k mixed tokens. That is what the
   "50k tokens" target is worth. **Below $0.01 only time counts.** Target therefore: cost ≤ $0.009 (margin),
   ≈ 50–65k tokens, then minimize seconds.
2. **Latency comes from output tokens.** On the critical path, keep every call ≤ 60 output tokens if possible. Run
   extraction as many small calls in parallel, never one long serial call. A fast-inference provider (Groq, below)
   cuts the per-token latency about 10×.

## 1. Target budgets (public dataset, sandbox)

| Phase | Today | Target | Main levers |
|---|---|---|---|
| Start + brief core | 2.8 s | ≤ 2.5 s | already split; output ≤ 60 tokens |
| Spec → requirements | 24 s | ≤ 15 s | frontier steps, gate form in 1 step, parallel pages, fetch reader |
| ERP | 108 s | ≤ 18 s after the requirements | prepared search hub, `search_many`, 3 frontier hops, fit table |
| Mail | 107 s | ≤ 20 s (off the critical path) | `search_many` over topics × folders, parallel message extraction |
| Tender + Q&A | 73 s | ≤ 15 s | parallel pager, iframe content via fetch reader |
| Submission after the evidence | 52 s | ≤ 22 s | bid form prepared up to the first position, form plan from position 1, code review check, TAN poll |
| **Total** | **184 s** | **≈ 55–60 s** | |
| Model calls | 229 | ≈ 60–70 (≈ 18 navigation, ≈ 6 submission, ≈ 40 small parallel extractions) | |
| Tokens | 830k | ≈ 50–65k, cost ≤ $0.01 | |

## 2. Architecture: a Fast Lane in front of the robust explorer that already exists

```
brief(core ‖ rest) ─┬─ SiteRunner(tender)   ─┐   each SiteRunner = Frontier Navigator (LLM) + Fast Reader + Extract Pool
                    ├─ SiteRunner(spec)     ─┤   checklists (existing *_progress) decide "complete"
                    ├─ SiteRunner(mail)     ─┤   gaps / errors / time-box → existing Explorer mission (fallback, unchanged)
                    └─ SiteRunner(erp) ◄────┘   (prepares its search hub before the groups are known)
   tender tab after its evidence: BidPrep (participation, bidder data, offer type) → waits at the first position
resolve (unchanged, deterministic) → FormPlanner(position 1) + replay(2..n) → conditions/declarations → TAN poll → submit
```

Principle: **the model picks every target. Code does the volume work in parallel.** This is within fair-play
clause 11: helpers extract model-selected pages, paginate model-selected lists and fill forms. The model chooses
each link, search term and form value. Nothing is crawled before the model decides.

### 2.1 Frontier Navigator (new; replaces the 1-tool-per-page loop in the fast lane)
- State per site: `opened` pages, a **frontier** (deduplicated links of all pages read so far, each with a short row
  or context label and a stable id like `L17`), and the **hub** (one interactive tab, shown in a pruned nav view).
- The prompt shows the goal, the checklist, *new* frontier items since the last step (older ones as a count), the
  hub nav view, and a one-line summary per background result.
- One JSON answer may hold several actions, executed in order with browser-use's stop rule (the remaining queue stops
  when the URL changes, an action fails, or an action is page-changing):
  `open[{id|ref, kind}]` (parallel helper reads plus background extraction; their links join the frontier) ·
  `paginate{ref, kind}` · `act[...]` (existing `steps`/`fill_fields`) · `search_many{ref, queries[], kind}` ·
  `go{id}` (moves the hub) · `look{question, ref}` (vision) · `wait` (returns with the next background result,
  i.e. P-3) · `done{missing[]}`.
- Navigation does **not** wait for extraction. A step returns as soon as the pages have loaded and their links are
  known.
- Reuse `Explorer._call` and the action methods of `site.py`, plus `_links` and `_next_link` from `explorer.py` and
  `_analogous` from `perf/fast`. New file `agent/rfq/agent/frontier.py`, about 300 lines.

### 2.2 Fast Reader (new; reads selected pages in about 0.2–0.5 s instead of 2.5 s)
- Mode A, `render`: the existing helper-tab `read_url`, kept but pooled. Warm tabs per site are reused instead of
  calling `new_page` every time, and guard checks run in one `evaluate`.
- Mode B, `fetch`: in the site's own tab, `fetch(url)` with the session cookies. The HTML goes into a
  **same-origin iframe with `sandbox="allow-same-origin"`, no scripts**, so stylesheets apply and computed-style decoy
  detection still works, but no dialogs, popups or gates run. Then `observe.js` serializes it. Nested iframes are
  resolved the same way.
- **Self-calibration per site, generic:** the first 2 reads of a site run both modes in parallel. If the serialized
  texts match (ignoring refs and whitespace), that site uses `fetch`. Otherwise it stays on `render`. Any `fetch`
  result that looks empty or dynamic (body under N characters, "JavaScript" notice, unlabelled canvas, a login form)
  falls back to `render` for that one read.
- Pagers with visible numbered page links are read **in parallel**. Otherwise read_all_pages follows the next link.
- Files: `agent/rfq/browser/reader.py` (new), small changes in `site.py` (`read_url` delegates to it).

### 2.3 Observation and context diet
- **Template subtraction:** lines seen on ≥ 2 earlier pages of the same site (navigation, footer, fake browser bar,
  recurring dialogs) are replaced by `[site chrome: n lines]`. This applies to the navigator *and* to extraction input.
- **Nav view** (Agent-E/AgentOccam): headings, controls, links with row context, short texts ≤ 120 characters,
  tables as `columns + first cells`, long texts as `[text, 1.4k chars: "first 60 chars…"]`. Extraction always
  gets the full text.
- Navigator system prompt ≈ 400 tokens (§6.1). No 20-tool JSON schema: one compact action grammar in JSON mode,
  about 1.5k tokens less per call.
- History: last 3 steps on one line each, plus the checklist. The checklist carries the state.

### 2.4 Extraction diet (output = latency)
- Schemas without copied prose: Q&A without `question`/`answer`, requirements without `original_text`, materials
  without `description`, mails without `body` **only if** the offline replay gate passes. X-4 failed once for mail
  draft flags, so mail may need an `is_draft` check with line references instead.
- Progress-aware: ask only for the fields still missing for an entity (already in d762e67 for materials).
  "Omit keys not on the page." `max_tokens` capped per kind.
- `EXTRACT_SYSTEM` on main grew to ≈ 900 tokens (eb540ab). Cut it to ≈ 120 tokens plus the kind schema.
- Many small parallel calls. Slots: `RFQ_LLM_PARALLEL` 10 → 24, with a priority lane for navigation and submission.
  This addresses the 228 s of slot waiting.
- Every extracted value must appear verbatim in the page text (code check, against hallucination). On a miss, one
  re-extraction.

### 2.5 Site playbooks: none. Generic behaviour that happens to be fast
- **Search fan-out** (`search_many`): the model names the input field and N queries. Code replays the search in N
  helper tabs, relocating the field by its descriptor (tag, name, label; `_FIELD_ID` in `site.py`). The result
  lists become frontier items. Mail: all topic queries, and the model adds folder variants in its next step. ERP: all
  catalogue groups at once.
- **Prepared hubs:** missions that wait for inputs (ERP waits for groups, mail for topics) navigate to their search
  hub in advance (X-6). It is the same LLM loop with a "prepare" goal.
- **Fit table for ERP:** code compares the attributes of the search rows with the requirements (`_mismatch` in
  `orchestrator.py`) and shows the result next to the frontier. The model decides which materials to open.
- **Resolver-driven completion:** the evidence phase ends when every checklist is complete *and* `resolve()` runs
  without gaps. Straggling decoy extractions are cancelled.

### 2.6 Submission ≤ 22 s after the evidence

### 6.1 Navigator system prompt (runtime, site-agnostic, ≈ 400 tokens)
```
You steer one website of a German B2B task (tender portal, supplier portal, ERP or webmail) to collect the facts in
the CHECKLIST. You choose where to go; code reads, extracts and fills for you, in parallel.
View: [eN]/[fNeM] = element refs of the HUB tab (valid until it changes). L<n> = links found on pages read so far
(FRONTIER), each with its row context. [info: …] tooltip, (disabled) locked, [img:/canvas:] text shown as picture.

The plan is written. No code was changed, and I left the branch Codex is working on (`codex/subminute-runtime`) alone. Plan file: `~/.claude/plans/we-are-with-our-jiggly-newell.md`.

**Where the time and tokens go today.** I pulled the platform data for your fastest `perf/fast` run (`run_1d8a967f…`: 100 points, 184.5 s, $0.094):
- **Calls:** 229 model calls, about 830k tokens in total.
- **Critical path:** the ERP phase alone runs from 24 s to 132 s, and the submission takes another 52 s after that.
- **Slow sites:** the first mail list only appears at 52 s; the first Q&A page at 62 s.
- **Waiting:** calls spent 228 s queued for one of the 10 model slots; 134 page reads took 2.5 s each.
- **Root cause:** about one model round trip per page per site. Trimming prompts can't fix that; the number of round trips has to drop about 8×.

**Two facts that set the strategy:**
1. **The ranking treats any cost below $0.01 as $0.01.** At Qwen prices, $0.01 is roughly 50–60k tokens, which is what your 50k target is really worth. Going below it gains nothing; only seconds count after that.
2. **Output tokens decide latency.** Each call takes about 1.4 s plus 13–20 ms per output token. So extraction should run as many small parallel calls, and every call on the critical path should stay short.

**The design ("Fast Lane"):** a new fast path in front of your current explorer, which stays as the fallback.
- **One model call picks many pages.** Each call sees every link found so far and chooses all the pages it needs at once; code opens them in parallel, extracts in the background, and the model doesn't wait for the extraction.
- **One search box, many queries.** The model names the search field and its queries; code runs them in parallel tabs. Mail covers every topic in one step, and ERP covers every catalogue group in one step.
- **Faster page reading.** Code downloads the selected page with the session cookies and lays it out with no scripts running. For each site, the first two pages are read both ways and compared; the fast way is only used if they match, and a page that looks incomplete falls back to a normal tab.
- **Smaller prompts and outputs.** Header and footer lines already seen on that site are dropped. The navigator sees a slimmed page view. Extraction no longer copies prose (Q&A answers, mail bodies) into its output.
- **Faster submission.** The bid form is filled up to the first position while evidence is still being collected. One call plans each new form page and the remaining positions are replayed by code. The review page is checked in code first, and the TAN is picked up by polling the inbox.
- **Fallback for unknown sites.** If a site's checklist is still incomplete after a time box, the existing explorer takes over. That keeps quality at 100 on the private dataset, at the cost of time.

**Expected result:**

| | Time | Tokens |
|---|---|---|
| Today (fastest run) | 184 s | ~830k |
| Fast Lane on Qwen | 65–75 s | ~50–65k |
| Fast Lane with a faster model provider | ≤ 60 s, reliably | ~50–65k |

These are estimates from the measured latencies, not measured results yet.

**Rollout:** five stages (measure, quick wins that are already built but switched off, faster page reading, the parallel navigator, then submission). Every stage is gated by unit tests, an offline check of the extraction changes, all 30 fake-portal cases at 100, and paired sandbox test runs. I also propose four new fake-portal profiles that attack the fast path specifically: JavaScript-only content, search results without their own URLs, information moved to another site, and pagers without page numbers.

The plan also contains two prompts I wrote: a ~400-token system prompt for the new navigator and a kickoff prompt for the implementing agent.

**Decision for you:** routing navigation and extraction through Groq, which the platform allows with your own key stored as a team secret. `gpt-oss-120b` runs at about 500 tokens/s for $0.15/$0.60 per million input/output tokens; `gpt-oss-20b` at about 1,000 tokens/s for $0.075/$0.30. That should take 20–30 s off the critical path while staying under the $0.01 floor. It costs real (small) money, and the platform proxy must accept the model, which we'd check first. Do you want that, or Qwen only?

Sources for the Groq figures: [CloudZero](https://www.cloudzero.com/blog/groq-pricing/), [computeprices.com](https://computeprices.com/providers/groq/models/gpt-oss-120b), [LosClouds](https://losclouds.com/ai-models/groq-gpt-oss-20b), [Artificial Analysis](https://artificialanalysis.ai/es/providers/groq), [AI Pricing Guru](https://www.aipricing.guru/blog/groq-api-pricing-guide-2026/).
